purpose: Strengthen v6.7 from one fixed transverse matroid to the complete transition matroid. Give two simple connected 4-regular Hamiltonian graphs related by one balanced mutation, hence having isomorphic full transition matroids by Traldi's characterization, while exhaustive colouring gives opposite 3-colourability verdicts.

balanced_mutation.reassembly: In the first pair swap the B-side half-edges, replacing 6-1 and 7-5 by 6-5 and 7-1. Leave the second pair reassembled as 4-2 and 9-3. No other edge changes.
balanced_mutation.result: The reassembled graph is exactly the positive graph. Both sides remain nonempty, every vertex keeps degree four, and the result is simple and connected. This is a balanced mutation in the standard four-edge-cut sense.

transition_matroid_theorem.source: Traldi's characterization: two 4-regular graphs have isomorphic transition matroids iff they are related by connected sums, separations and balanced mutations.
transition_matroid_theorem.application: The displayed pair differs by one balanced mutation. Therefore M_tau(G_negative) is isomorphic to M_tau(G_positive).
transition_matroid_theorem.strong_scope: Unlike v6.7, this conclusion concerns the entire transition matroid, not merely the transverse matroid of one chosen circuit partition.

exact_verification: Both edge lists are simple connected 4-regular graphs on ten vertices.
The displayed Hamiltonian cycles use graph edges and visit all ten vertices exactly once before returning to the start.
The symmetric edge difference is exactly {1-6,5-7} removed and {1-7,5-6} added, matching the stated balanced mutation.
Exhaustive enumeration of all 3^10 colour assignments gives zero proper 3-colourings for the negative graph and exactly 18 for the positive graph.

main_theorem.name: THREE_COLORABILITY_IS_NOT_AN_INVARIANT_OF_THE_FULL_TRANSITION_MATROID
main_theorem.statement: There exist simple connected 4-regular Hamiltonian graphs G and G' with isomorphic full transition matroids but chi(G)>3 and chi(G')<=3.
proof: The explicit four-edge-cut reassembly is a balanced mutation, so Traldi's theorem gives M_tau(G) isomorphic to M_tau(G').
The checker verifies Hamiltonicity and 4-regularity of both graphs directly.
The checker exhausts all 59049 three-colour assignments on each graph, finding zero for G and eighteen for G'.
Hence full transition-matroid isomorphism does not preserve the 3-colourability decision bit.

killed: Any exact 3-colourability solver whose complete instance representation factors only through the isomorphism class of the full transition matroid.

Any complete decision criterion expressed solely through invariants of M_tau that are necessarily preserved under transition-matroid isomorphism, including arbitrary evaluations of a transition-matroid Tutte polynomial.
The hope that upgrading v6.7 from one transverse matroid to the whole transition matroid restores the lost colouring information.
not_killed: Graph data together with a transition matroid, when the extra data distinguishes balanced-mutation representatives.
Hamiltonian cyclic-order / embedding / gain information that is not invariant under the displayed mutation.
Direct GF(3) tension algorithms using the actual incidence structure.

next_target.name: E8_BALANCED_MUTATION_SENSITIVE_HAMILTONIAN_ORDER_INVARIANT_V6_9
next_target.directive: Stop treating transition/isotropic matroids as complete instance carriers. Identify the smallest polynomial-size Hamiltonian-order or GF(3)-gain datum changed by the v6.8 mutation and prove how it enters the nowhere-zero tension test. Seek a contraction sensitive to this datum while retaining the exact Hamiltonian source structure. Mandatory control: it must distinguish the v6.8 pair and still avoid assignment/sign enumeration.

sources: Lorenzo Traldi, The transition matroid of a 4-regular graph: an introduction, European Journal of Combinatorics 50 (2015), 180-207; Theorem 6 characterizes isomorphic transition matroids by connected sums, separations and balanced mutations.
